In my [previous post](/posts/01-ai-board-of-directors/), I introduced my "Board of Directors" composed of AI agents. The concept is seductive on paper: getting virtual experts to collaborate on designing the ultimate training plan.

But in engineering, we all know that **"Theory is when you know everything but nothing works."**

Having a plan generated by an AI isn't enough. It has to be executable, secure, and adapted to my actual physical constraints. I’m not a certified coach, but I have experience (40 pro Muay Thai fights) and I know how to read the documentation. So, I treated this AI-generated plan like a critical **Pull Request**.

I subjected it to a ruthless **Code Review**, confronting the Generator (Gemini) with an Adversarial Agent (ChatGPT), industry standards (Joe Friel), and my own "Ground Truth."

Here is the "Design Time" for my 2026 season.

## 1. Legacy Code Audit: Lambo Engine, 2CV Chassis

To generate this plan, I didn't want a generic template. I fed the model **3 years of logs** (Strava/Garmin exports). The AI started with an audit of the "Legacy System" (my body) and detected two major issues.

### A. Observability Failure (The 100k Post-Mortem)
The AI replayed the logs from my previous preparation (a stock plan bought on TrainingPeaks for a 100k race in December). It spotted an anomaly (bug) that I had missed at the time: a brutal and continuous drop in HRV (Heart Rate Variability) at the end of an assimilation block.
**The Diagnostic:** Bad polarization. I started the next block already "fried."
**The Result:** Injury and failure (DNF).
**The Lesson:** The new system must integrate strict HRV monitoring to avoid this system crash.

### B. Hardware Specs
Gemini dropped a stinging metaphor that became the cornerstone of my entire planning:

> **"Coach Trail (Gemini):** You have a Lamborghini engine mounted on a Citroën 2CV chassis."

**Translation:** My cardio engine (acquired through years of Muay Thai and sports) is massive. It doesn't "drift" even over 20 hours of effort.
However, my mechanical structure (tendons, feet, plantar fascia) is the **Single Point of Failure (SPOF)**. If I run as much as my engine allows, I break the chassis.

## 2. System Architecture: Load Balancing

To bypass this bottleneck (plantar fasciitis), the AI proposed a strong architectural decision: **Load Balancing**.

Instead of betting everything on running (high impact), the plan shifts a massive load of the aerobic volume to a third-party "Micro-service": **Cycling (Home Trainer)**.

![Weekly Volume Planning - Bike vs Run](1000005422.jpg)

* **Blue (Bike):** We build the base and maintain engine displacement without wearing out the disks (the feet).
* **Orange (Run):** We switch to specificity (running) only when approaching "Production Deployments" (intermediate races and the final objective).

This is a **Predictive Maintenance** strategy: preserving hardware for D-Day.

## 3. Compliance Testing: The "Friel" Standard

Before even starting the debate with the Adversarial agent, I ran the plan against an absolute reference: **Joe Friel** (author of *The Triathlete's Training Bible*). To me, this book is the "Official Documentation" (RFC) of endurance engineering.

I checked if the code generated by Gemini complied with Friel's fundamental **Specs**, particularly the principle of **Specificity** (*"The closer you get to the event, the more the training must resemble it"*).

**The Compliance Test:**

* **"Dev" Phase (Start of cycle):** We work on general capacities far removed from the race.
    * *Check:* February/March are packed with short VO2Max and Max Strength. It’s very intense, but very far from an Ultra effort. -> **✅ PASS.**
* **"Prod" Phase (End of cycle):** We converge towards specificity.
    * *Check:* The closer we get to December (Chiang Mai), the more VO2Max disappears in favor of pure volume and specific pacing (Zone 1/Zone 2). The training environment becomes identical to the race environment. -> **✅ PASS.**

If the AI had scheduled 400m sprints in November (1 month before the 160km), the test would have failed (`Compliance Error`). Here, the logic of progressivity is respected to the letter.

## 4. The Adversarial Code Review

This is the most critical part. I do not blindly trust the LLM. I use a second LLM (ChatGPT) in "Adversarial" mode to challenge Gemini's choices. Here are two examples of technical "Debates" that shaped the plan.

### Case A: The 4:1 Cycle (Bug or Feature?)

Reading the plan, I flagged an issue. The academic standard is 3 weeks of load for 1 week of recovery (3:1). Gemini scheduled **4-week load cycles**.

**🧑‍💻 Me (The Dev):** *"Why 4 weeks? It’s risky. The Friel standard is 3:1."*

**🤖 Gemini (The Architect):** *"This is **Functional Overload**. Since you are a Hybrid profile (50% cycling), your joints don't suffer the impact stress of a pure runner. We can therefore stretch the load cycle to build a deeper base without breaking."*

**🕵️‍♂️ ChatGPT (The Reviewer):** *"The argument is technically sound. Cycling reduces mechanical stress. **HOWEVER**, this is valid only if you have real-time monitoring. If HRV drops or RPE spikes, you must cut the cycle, even if the plan says 'Week 4'."*

**Verdict:** ✅ **Merged.** I accepted the 4:1 cycle, but with a strict monitoring condition (HRV + Morning Readiness). It’s dynamic piloting, not static.

### Case B: The Case of the "Missing VO2Max"

Analyzing Phase 4 (Specific Prep for 100 Miles), I spotted what I thought was a critical hallucination.

**🧑‍💻 Me:** *"There is no VO2Max or Threshold work after August? I’m going to get slow and my running economy will collapse."*

**🤖 Gemini:** *"It’s a **Feature**, not a bug. For a 100 Miler, we want a Diesel engine, not an F1. If we add VO2Max (Stress A) on top of Ultra Volume (Stress B), the cup overflows. We replace Cardio Intensity with Strength Endurance (Hills)."*

I was skeptical. I asked for a "Second Opinion" from the Adversarial agent.

**🕵️‍♂️ ChatGPT:** *"The 'Diesel' logic is good for safety. But your fear is grounded: cutting intensity completely can degrade your running economy and muscle tension."*

I sent this feedback back to Gemini. Its response was a masterclass in **Refactoring**.

**🤖 Gemini (Refined Strategy):** *"Ok, validated. We apply a **Hybrid Strategy**:*
1.  *We keep VO2Max/Power, but **exclusively on the bike** (Zero impact, maintenance of VO2Max).*
2.  *On foot, we do Tempo on hills (Zone 3) and 'Eccentric loading' on active downhills."*

![Heart Rate Zone Distribution Patched](1000005442.png)
*The final result (v1.1): You can clearly see the intensity reminders (orange/red) maintained thanks to this negotiation.*

**Verdict:** ✅ **Merged with Refactoring.** The plan is robust thanks to this ping-pong.

## Conclusion: Ready to Deploy?

At the end of this "Design Time" phase, I have a plan that:
1.  Respects my Hardware constraints (2CV Chassis).
2.  Passed the Physiological Unit Tests (Friel Standard, Polarization).
3.  Was validated by a contradictory review (Adversarial Agent).

Everything looks perfect on paper. But as every developer knows, **nothing survives first contact with Production.**

As early as the second week, I suffered a critical incident: an ankle sprain followed by an illness. In the next article (Part 3), I will show you how the AI handles **"Run Time"**, medical Hotfixes, and dynamic adaptation.

*Stay tuned.*
